title: Basic Data Analysis Oral Assessment
instructions: Answer each question in your own words. You may correct transcription errors before accepting each answer. The examiner does not provide hints or model answers.

questions.prompt: In your own words, what is the difference between numerical data and categorical data? Give one example of each.
If you have a set of values, when would the mean be useful, and when might the median give a better description?
What does the spread or variability of data tell you? Name one measure of spread if you know one.
Suppose one value in a data set is much larger than all the others. How could that outlier affect the mean and the median?
When you look at a histogram, what features would you examine to understand the distribution of the data?
Why do we often use a sample instead of measuring an entire population, and what can make a sample misleading?
If two variables have a strong correlation, can we conclude that one causes the other? Explain your reasoning.
Imagine a scatter plot where points generally rise from left to right but are widely scattered. What would you say about the relationship?
A data set has missing values and some obvious data-entry errors. What should you do before analysing it?
You compare two groups and find that their averages are different. What else would you want to know before concluding that the groups are meaningfully different?
